questions.question: Which three structural requirements turn a binary operation into a group operation?
options: Commutativity, an identity, and inverses
Associativity, commutativity, and an identity
Associativity, inverses, and distributivity
Associativity, an identity, and inverses

questions.question: In a group, if $ab=ac$, what can you conclude?
options: $b=c$
$a=e$
nothing can be concluded

questions.question: Which group axiom fails for the natural numbers $\{0,1,2,\ldots\}$ under addition?
options: Sums of two natural numbers can leave the set.
Additive inverses are not in the set.
Addition is not commutative on the set.
Addition fails to be associative there.

questions.question: Why is $(\mathbb{Z},+)$ a group?
options: Addition is associative, with identity $1$ and inverse $1/a$ for each $a$.
Addition is associative, with identity $0$ and inverse $-a$ for each $a$.
Addition is commutative and closed, which is all a group requires.
Addition is associative with identity $0$; inverses are not needed.

questions.question: Is $(\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\},\cdot)$ a group?
options: Yes, since it has identity $1$ and is associative; inverses are not needed.
No, because some products of nonzero reals are equal to zero.
Yes, every nonzero real number has reciprocal inverse.
No, because $0$ is missing and must be the identity.

questions.question: What extra condition makes a group Abelian?
options: Existence of an identity element.
Existence of inverse elements.
Associativity of the group operation.
Commutativity of the group operation.

questions.question: In the additive group $\mathbb{Z}_5$, what is the inverse of $4$?
Does $\{1,-1,i,-i\}$ form a group under complex multiplication?
options: Yes, products stay in the set and each element has an inverse there
No, because $i\cdot i=-1$ is real and not one of the imaginary elements
Yes, because it is a subset of the group $(\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\},\cdot)$, and subsets of groups are groups
No, because the negative elements $-1$ and $-i$ have no inverses in the set

questions.question: In a group with operation $\star$ and identity $e$, how many inverses can an element $a$ have?
options: Exactly one inverse.
At least one inverse, possibly several.
Exactly one, but only if the group is Abelian.
Exactly one, but only if the group is finite.

questions.question: Why is $\{0,1\}$ under multiplication not a group?
options: The set is finite, so it cannot contain all inverses.
Multiplication on $\{0,1\}$ is not associative.
The element $0$ has no multiplicative inverse.
The element $1$ has no inverse, since $1\cdot0=0$.
